Abu Dhabi, the capital city of the United Arab Emirates, is recognized as both a metropolis and a municipality. It covers a total area of 972.0 square kilometers and is situated at an elevation of 27.0 meters above sea level. The city has a population of 1,512,000 and operates within the time zone known as Time in the United Arab Emirates, with a UTC offset of +4.

As the seat of government, Abu Dhabi is home to the Cabinet of the United Arab Emirates, which has its headquarters in the city. The United Arab Emirates Navy and the French Navy both have their garrisons located in Abu Dhabi. The city also serves as the jurisdiction for the Abu Dhabi Urban Planning Council and is the location of the headquarters for organizations such as Quest Arabiya and Romai Sports.

Abu Dhabi is a significant center for education and research, hosting the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence and serving as a campus location for Al Ain University. The city is also the region for major medical institutions like Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and Sheikh Khalifa Medical City.

Several notable events have taken place in Abu Dhabi, including the 2009 and 2010 FIFA Club World Cup Finals and the 2019 AFC Asian Cup match between Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. The city is also the site of the Zayed Sports City Stadium, which is operated by Abu Dhabi.

Abu Dhabi is a hub for various companies and organizations. Caracal International, Emirates Defence Industries Company, and Adcom Systems are all based in the city, while Waha Capital lists Abu Dhabi as its location country. The city is also served by DHL International Aviation ME, which targets its airport. Additionally, Aldar Properties, Fakhro Group, and DeSimone Consulting Engineers serve the Abu Dhabi region.

The city is associated with several prominent individuals. Robert Renwick, Samir El-Mais, and Benny Dayal were born in Abu Dhabi, while Begum Dolly Azad, Jouan Salem Al Dhaheri, and Sadiq al-Mahdi passed away there. Danielle Piermatei resides in Abu Dhabi, and Maciej Matthew Szymanski is known for his connection to the city. Basil Al Bayati has received an award from Abu Dhabi.

Abu Dhabi is also the location for Capital Gate and Capital Plaza, as well as the setting for the television programme Capital Connection. The city is home to the headquarters of Romai Sports and Quest Arabiya. Furthermore, the Al Wathba Wetland Reserve is located near Abu Dhabi, and the city is the region served by both Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and Sheikh Khalifa Medical City. The headquarters of the Cabinet of the United Arab Emirates and the garrisons of the United Arab Emirates Navy and the French Navy are also situated in Abu Dhabi.

Accra, the capital and largest city of Ghana, is also recognized as a metropolis and serves as the capital for the Gold Coast (British colony) and is referenced in the history of Ghana as its capital. The city is situated at an elevation of 60.96 meters and operates within the GMT time zone, with a UTC offset of +0. Accra covers a total area of 20.4 square kilometers, while its urban area spans 199,400,000.0 square meters and the metropolitan area extends to 3,245,000,000.0 square meters. The population of the city itself is 284,124, whereas the metropolitan population reaches 5,455,692. Residents of Accra are known as Accrans. The city uses the area code 030 and postal codes GA, GL, and GZ.

Accra is located in Ghana and is also associated with Sub-Saharan Africa. The Ga and Dangme languages are spoken in the city. Several institutions and organizations are based in Accra, including the Ministry of Women and Children's Affairs, Bishop Bowers School, Braves of Customs, and the headquarters of the Progress Party (Ghana), Meridian Airways, and Metro TV (Ghana). The Environmental Protection Agency (Ghana), Ghana Airports Company Limited, and Ghana News Agency are also located in the city.

Accra is home to educational institutions such as Sikkim Manipal University, Ghana Learning Centre, and Wisconsin International University College. The Presbyterian Senior High School, Osu, and Sarbah Hall are situated in the city, as is Uniiq FM. The city serves as the garrison for the President's Own Guard Regiment, the Ghana Regiment, and the West Africa Command. Sports teams such as Accra Great Olympics F.C. (2020–21 season), Vision F.C., and Liberty Professionals F.C. play their home games in Accra.

The city is the location or birthplace of several notable individuals, including Prince Amponsah, Prince Baffoe, and Prince Gyasi. It is also the place where Carl Henry Clerk, Prince Yawson, and Roger Joseph Felli passed away. Accra is the hometown of Samini, Barima Sidney, and Becca, the Ghanaian singer. Juliet Ibrahim has received an award in Accra.

Nearby natural attractions include Achimota Forest and Shai Hills Resource Reserve, both of which are closest to Accra. The city is served by companies such as GIG Mobility, Surfline Communications, and BusyInternet. Notable residents include Benjamin Asante, Derek Abrefa, and Kwesi Amissah-Arthur.

Islamabad, the federal capital of Pakistan, was founded on August 14, 1967. It serves as the capital not only for Pakistan but also for West Pakistan and the former administrative units of Pakistan. The city is governed by the Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation and is located within the country’s Pakistan Standard Time zone, with a UTC offset of +05:00. Residents of Islamabad are known as Islamabadi, and the city uses the area code 051 and the postal code 44000.

Covering a total area of 220.0 square kilometers, Islamabad has an urban area of 220,150,000.0 square meters and a metropolitan area of 1,165,500,000.0 square meters. The total population stands at 1,009,832, with a metropolitan population of 2,003,368 and a population density of 2,089.0 people per square kilometer.

Islamabad is home to several important institutions and organizations. The Cabinet Secretariat (Pakistan), the Capital Development Authority (Islamabad), and the Public-Private Partnership Authority (Pakistan) all have their headquarters in the city. The Capital Talk program is also based in Islamabad. The city serves as the garrison for the President's Bodyguard (Pakistan), the Corona Relief Tiger Force, and the Pakistan Air Force. Additionally, the Utility Stores Corporation, Hashoo Group, and Islamabad Electric Supply Company are located in Islamabad.

The city is a significant educational hub, hosting campuses of the University of Lahore, Pakistan Institute of Public Finance Accountants, and Al-Hamd Islamic University. Preston University (Pakistan) and Pak-Turk Maarif International Schools & Colleges are also situated in Islamabad. The Capital University of Science & Technology and Quaid-i-Azam University are among the prominent institutions located in the city.

Islamabad has been the site of notable events such as the Siege of Lal Masjid and has hosted the Quaid-e-Azam Inter Provincial Youth Games. The 1977 and 2008 Pakistani general elections in Islamabad were significant political events in the city’s history.

Several notable individuals are associated with Islamabad. Rohail Nazir, Sarmad Tariq, and Humaira Bano were born in the city, while Qazi Hussain Ahmad, Rufin Anthony, and Samina Raja passed away there. Qayaas, Adil Omar, and Faakhir Mehmood consider Islamabad their hometown. Qaiser Mushtaq, Qamar Zaman Chaudhry, and Roedad Khan reside in the city. Constantinos Apostolou Doxiadis played a significant role in the development of Islamabad as a major project.

Islamabad is also the location of France Colony, which is classified as a type of Islamabad area. The city is the nearest urban center to Margalla Hills National Park and is served by the Quaid-e-Azam International Hospital. The Islamabad Chamber of Commerce & Industry, Islamabad Football Association, and Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation all serve the region. Model Town Humak operates under the government type of Islamabad.

Aasim Sajjad Akhtar is noted for his occupation in Islamabad. The city is also the site of the campus for the University of Lahore, Pakistan Institute of Public Finance Accountants, and Al-Hamd Islamic University. The Capital University of Science & Technology and Quaid-i-Azam University are located in Islamabad, and the city is the region served by the Islamabad Chamber of Commerce & Industry, Islamabad Football Association, and Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation.

Lagos, located in Nigeria, is the country's largest city and also holds this distinction within the African Union and during the period of military dictatorship in Nigeria. It serves as the capital of Colonial Nigeria, the Federation of Nigeria, and Lagos Colony. The city covers a total area of 1,171.28 square kilometers, with a land area of 999.6 square kilometers, an urban area of 907 square kilometers, and a metropolitan area spanning 2,706.7 square kilometers. Water bodies account for 171.68 square kilometers of its area. Lagos sits at an elevation of 41.148 meters above sea level.

The population of Lagos is significant, with 8,048,430 residents in the city proper and a metropolitan population of 21,320,000. The population density stands at 6,871 people per square kilometer in the city and 7,759 per square kilometer in the metropolitan area. Residents of Lagos are known as Lagosians. The city operates in the West Africa Time zone, with a UTC offset of +1, and uses the area code 010. Its motto is "Èkó ò ní bàjé o!" The Awori tribe is recognized as the founder of Lagos.

Lagos is a major hub for various organizations and activities. The Benfruit Plant, the Nigerian Institute of Management, and the television series "Before 30" are all located in the city. The Reduction of Lagos took place here, and it is the birthplace of notable individuals such as Cait O'Riordan, Candy Augustine Agbane, and actress Carol King. It is also the place where Amusa Shittu, Samuel Ajayi Crowther, and Samuel Johnson, the Nigerian historian, passed away.

Several companies, including Dobox and IROKO Partners, were founded in Lagos. The city features significant buildings designed by Isaac Fola-Alade and Olufemi Majekodunmi, and Isaac Fola-Alade is also known for important projects in Lagos. The city is a key aviation center, serving as the target airport for Cally Air, Ibom Air, and Max Air, and as the hub airport for ADC Airlines.

Educational institutions such as Babington Macaulay Junior Seminary, Government College Ikorodu, and Ebun Oluwa Pro Veritas are located in Lagos State. The city is also the assembly site for vehicles like the Volkswagen Beetle, Volkswagen Jetta (A2), and Isuzu Forward. The Benin-Ore-Shagamu Expressway, Encomium Magazine, and Bogobiri House are all associated with Lagos.

Lagos is the location city for the United Africa Company of Nigeria, Promasidor Nigeria, and G-Worldwide Entertainment, and serves as the location country for LADOL. The Atlantic Ocean and Lagos Lagoon are the nearest major bodies of water to the city. Several songs, including "Let Me Roll It," "Mamunia," and "Band on the Run," were recorded in Lagos.

The First Consultant Hospital and the National Orthopaedic Hospital, Igbobi, are situated in the Lagos region. GIG Mobility and TEDxLagos serve the Lagos region as well. The city is home to the headquarters of Caritas Communications, the Nigerian Accounting Association, and Merchant Express Aviation. MFM F.C., ACB Lagos F.C., and COD United F.C. all play their home games in Lagos.

Lagos is the hometown of Sasha P, Davina Oriakhi, and VanJess, and is known for individuals such as Olu Amoda and Toki Mabogunje. Desmond Majekodunmi, Buchi Emecheta, and Habeeb Okunola received their education in Lagos. Patrick Utomi, Dakuku Peterside, and Mudashiru Obasa reside in the city. Juliet Ibrahim has received an award in Lagos.

Finally, Sub-Saharan Africa lists Lagos as a country, and the city is the state for several educational institutions. The city is also the region for important hospitals and serves as a region for various organizations and events.

Aneurin Bevan served as deputy to Hugh Gaitskell during Gaitskell's second tenure. Bevan was also the predecessor to Alfred Robens, Baron Robens of Woldingham, in Robens's second tenure, and to Hilary Marquand in Marquand's first tenure. In addition, Bevan was succeeded by Jim Griffiths in Griffiths's second tenure, by Henry Willink in Willink's first tenure, and by George Isaacs in Isaacs's second tenure. Beyond his professional roles, Aneurin Bevan was married to Jennie Lee, Baroness Lee of Asheridge.

Anthony Giddens, whose birth name is also Anthony Giddens and who is sometimes known as Tony Giddens, was born in London on January 18, 1938. He is associated with the Labour Party in the United Kingdom. Giddens is the author of "The Transformation of Intimacy." His work has had a significant influence on several scholars, including Stephen R. Barley, Wanda Orlikowski, and Alexander Wendt.

Antoine Lavoisier was born in Paris on August 26, 1743. He pursued his education at the University of Paris and the Collège des Quatre-Nations, ultimately establishing himself as a chemist. Lavoisier was notably influenced by Guillaume-François Rouelle and Étienne Condillac, and he, in turn, influenced figures such as Andrés Manuel del Río. His contributions to science include significant work on the carbon cycle, elemental analysis, and hydrogen. Lavoisier was the author of "Traité Élémentaire de Chimie." He was married to Marie-Anne Paulze Lavoisier. Lavoisier died in the French First Republic on May 8, 1794, with the cause of death being execution by guillotine.

Antonio Negri was born in Padua on August 1, 1933. He is associated with Western philosophy and has been notably influenced by thinkers such as Galvano Della Volpe and Karl Marx. Negri is the author of "Multitude: War and Democracy in the Age of Empire." His influence extends to figures like Franco Berardi, and he also appeared in the film "Marx Reloaded."
